page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.48xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8gb.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance and memory throughput. Multi-core stress-ng tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the top 10% of performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 21328.86 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 434.92 GB/sec. Single-core performance, such as single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores, sits in the average tier. The system also excels in database operations and static web serving throughput, both ranking in the top 10% of tested servers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core density and dedicated CPU allocation offer excellent compute-per-resource value for parallelized workloads, though the lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage solutions. The instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput static web serving. It is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring local high-speed SSDs or GPU acceleration.
